source_text: Postquam autem vir naturali appetitu cognovit uxorem, dicit Scriptura divina: Concepit Eva et peperit filium, et vocavit nomen eius Cain. Sed quid dicit Adam audiamus: Adquisivi hominem per Deum 29. Unde constat opus Dei esse, quem per Deum adquisitum Scriptura divina testatur
pass_a_gloss: After the man knew his wife by natural appetite, divine Scripture says: Eve conceived and bore a son, and called his name Cain. But let us hear what Adam says: I have acquired a human being through God. Whence it is established that he is God's work, whom divine Scripture testifies was acquired through God.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature

pass_b_english: After the man knew his wife through natural appetite, divine Scripture says: “Eve conceived and bore a son, and called his name Cain.” But let us hear what Adam says: “I have acquired a human being through God” (Genesis 4:1). This establishes that the person whom divine Scripture testifies was acquired through God is God’s work.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
